newsitem.title: USA: United Dominion,South West to merge.
newsitem.headline: United Dominion,South West to merge.

text.p: United Dominion Realty Trust Inc and South West Property Trust Inc said Tuesday they have agreed to merge. Under the deal, South West shareholders would receive about $312 million of United Dominion common stock.
The merger is expected to immediately boost funds from operations per share, the company said.

Under the terms of the agreement, each share of South West will be exchanged for 1.0833 shares of United Dominion provided that United Dominion's average closing price during the pricing period is $13-7/8 or higher.
If the average closing price falls below that level, the exchange ratio will be adjusted upward to provide a $15 value for each South West share, the company said.
The exchange ratio assures South West stockholders that their current dividend rate will not be reduced, it said.
United Dominion said it is not required to offer more than 1.1215 shares, and South West is not required to accept less than $15 per share in value.
The merger is expected to be completed at the close of business on December 31.

Three of South West's executives - Chairman and Chief Executive John Schneider, President and Chief Operating Officer Robert Sherman and Executive Vice President and Chief Investment Officer David Johnston - are to join United Dominion as executive officers.
Schneider, as well as three South West directors - Mark Sandler, Robert Scharar and Ira Wender - also will be joining United Dominion's board of directors.
